## The running example (for reference)

| | |
|---|---|
| **P** — Population | Adults (18+) with septic shock in the ICU |
| **I** — Intervention | Restrictive fluid strategy |
| **C** — Comparison | Usual care (standard fluids) |
| **O** — Outcome | Death from any cause |
| **T** — Time | Within 28 days |

**Question:** *In adults with septic shock in the ICU, does a restrictive fluid strategy, compared with usual care, reduce 28-day mortality?*

## Exercise 1 — From clinical scenario to PICO(T)  *(warm-up on your own 3 minutes, then pairs 8 minutes)*

**Warm-up — spot the PICO** *(on your own, 3 minutes)*

*"In adults aged 65+ after hip-fracture surgery, does a daily non-drug bundle, compared with usual care, reduce delirium in the first 7 days?"*

| P | I | C | O | T |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| | | | | |

**Pair task.** Pick **ONE** scenario. Fill the PICO(T) boxes, then write the question as **one sentence**.

**Tips**
- For an observational question, **I** becomes **E** (exposure) — "PECO".
- A descriptive question (how many? how often?) may only need **P** and **O**.
- Choose **one** primary outcome and say **when** it is measured.

**Scenario A — Ventilator-associated pneumonia.** Your ICU raises the head of the bed to 30–45° for ventilated patients, but compliance is patchy at night. A colleague wonders whether a twice-daily nurse checklist would reduce ventilator-associated pneumonia.

**Scenario B — Pressure injuries.** Several patients in your medical ward developed pressure injuries last quarter. Some staff turn patients every 2 hours, others every 4 hours. Nobody knows how often pressure injuries occur in your unit.

**Scenario C — Delirium.** Older patients after hip-fracture surgery often become confused. The geriatric team suggests a daily non-drug bundle (glasses and hearing aids on, orientation, sleep protection, early mobilisation).

**Scenario D — Stroke door-to-needle time.** Your emergency department wants to know whether a pre-hospital alert from the ambulance shortens the time from arrival to thrombolysis.

**Scenario E — Medication errors.** The pharmacy notices many errors when patients move from ICU to the ward. They propose a pharmacist-led medication reconciliation at transfer.

| | My scenario: ___ |
|---|---|
| **P** — who? | |
| **I / E** — what is given or what are they exposed to? | |
| **C** — compared with what? | |
| **O** — which outcome? | |
| **T** — measured when? | |

**My question in one sentence:**

______________________________________________________________________________

______________________________________________________________________________

**Type of question** (tick one): ☐ descriptive  ☐ analytical — observational  ☐ analytical — experimental

## Exercise 2 — FINER traffic light  *(pairs, part of the same 8 minutes; Part B is extra practice)*

**Part A.** Rate *your* question from Exercise 1. Colour or write **G** (green — fine), **A** (amber — needs thought) or **R** (red — must change).

| Letter | Test | G / A / R | Why? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F** — Feasible | Enough patients, time, money, skills, data? | | |
| **I** — Interesting | To you, your team and readers? | | |
| **N** — Novel | Confirms, refutes or extends what is known? | | |
| **E** — Ethical | Could an ethics committee approve it? | | |
| **R** — Relevant | Could the answer change practice, policy or research? | | |

If any letter is **red**, rewrite the question here:

______________________________________________________________________________

**Part B (if time).** Which FINER letter is the main problem in each question below?

1. "In all hospitalised adults in our country, does vitamin D supplementation reduce mortality over 10 years?" — Main problem: ______
2. "In ICU patients with septic shock, does withholding antibiotics for 24 hours reduce resistance?" — Main problem: ______
3. "Do nurses in our ICU wash their hands?" (already measured monthly by the infection-control audit for 5 years) — Main problem: ______
4. "In adults with community-acquired pneumonia, does the colour of the drug chart affect 28-day mortality?" — Main problem: ______

## Exercise 4 — Proposal builder 1  *(group, 28 minutes)*

Write your answers into the **Research Proposal template** (`Templates/Research_Proposal_Template.docx`), Part 1. This sheet is your checklist. The search, references, problem statement and working title are **tomorrow** (Proposal builder 2).

**Suggested roles:** chair · scribe (types into the template) · timekeeper · "devil's advocate" (checks FINER).

| Time | Task | Done |
|---|---|---|
| 0–7 min | **1. Choose ONE problem** from your unit: list 3 ideas, vote, pick one | ☐ |
| 7–14 min | **2. PICO(T) table** and the **research question** in one sentence | ☐ |
| 14–19 min | **3. FINER check** — traffic light for every letter; rewrite the question if any letter is red | ☐ |
| | **4. Research, audit or QI?** Write the approval route (ethics committee or local approval) | ☐ |
| 19–25 min | **5. Aim** (one sentence), **2–3 objectives** (measurable verbs; mark the primary), **H0 / H1** (or "descriptive — no hypothesis") | ☐ |
| 25–28 min | One group reads its question and aim aloud; the room suggests one improvement | ☐ |

**Our question:** ________________________________________________________________

**FINER:** F ☐  I ☐  N ☐  E ☐  R ☐  (G / A / R)      **Type:** ☐ research ☐ audit ☐ QI

**Quality checks before you stop**
- [ ] Every PICO box is filled, and there is only **one** primary outcome with a time point.
- [ ] The question, aim, primary objective and hypothesis all talk about the **same** outcome.
- [ ] No FINER letter is red.
- [ ] You know whether it is research, audit or QI, and who must approve it.
